content.text: {"persuasion":"PERSUADED","support_scope":"CORE_ONLY","rationale":"The entry is about what 'Egypt' names when Scripture uses it as a spiritual name, and the decisive text is Revelation 11:8, which explicitly attaches the name to 'the great city... where also our Lord was crucified.' Only one city answers that clause: Jerusalem. The book supplies the mechanism the common interpretation itself concedes — Egypt is 'the house of bondage' (Exod 20:2) — and shows Paul applying exactly that predicate to 'Jerusalem which now is... in bondage with her children' (Gal 4:25). It further shows the prophetic precedent for renaming Jerusalem by a wicked city's name (Isa 1:10, rulers of Sodom; Ezek 16:46), so the method is native to Scripture, not invented. The blood-of-prophets criterion (Rev 18:24) matches Jesus' fixed address for that blood (Matt 23:35–37; Luke 13:33). The strongest rival — Rev 11:8's great city as Rome or the generic God-opposing world-system, with Egypt as a free-floating symbol of oppression — must spiritualize 'where also our Lord was crucified' against its plain force, has no answer for the Gal 4:25 bondage link, and ignores the Isa 1:10 precedent of the prophets calling Jerusalem by Sodom's name. The common interpretation (Egypt = bondage to sin) is not actually denied by the book; it is the semantic engine of the identification. However, the printed entry also folds in 'the whore of Babylon that rides the beast,' a larger and more contested equation defended in ch. 35; that elaboration faces real unanswered objections (e.g., Rev 17:18's city 'which reigneth over the kings of the earth') and should not be treated as established by this entry's evidence. The core — Egypt as a spiritual name for Jerusalem in Rev 11:8 — is the best-supported explanation of the supplied texts.","book_core_identification":"When Scripture uses 'Egypt' as a spiritual name
